items.title: Writing Logical Statements With Quantifiers (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: Writing Logical Statements With Quantifiers with the Class Activity and a self-check (PDF 33, printed 29).

blocks.text: Quantifiers se hum library ke aam qaide likh sakte hain. Maslan ∀x, Student(x) → Borrows(x, Book) ka matlab hai “har student ek kitab leta hai.” ∃y, Book(y) ∧ Available(y) ka matlab hai “kam az kam ek kitab aisi hai jo dastiyab (available) hai.” Yeh statements qaide aur shartein theek theek tay karte hain. Quantifiers se library system ki aam suratein bhi aur khaas suratein bhi bayan hoti hain.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Nishaan parhne ka tareeqa: → ko “agar ... to” parhein, ∧ ko “aur” (AND). Pehle qaide mein kitab ne “Book” likha hai jis ka matlab yahan “koi kitab” hai. Poori baqaida shakal yeh hogi: ∀x, Student(x) → (∃y, Book(y) ∧ Borrows(x, y)).

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Students “Tamam students ka class mein aana zaroori hai” jaise qaide universal quantifier (∀) se likhein.

blocks.prompt: Qaida “Har dastiyab kitab li ja sakti hai” quantifier se likhein, aur dastiyab kitab B7 ke baare mein faisla karein.
blocks.explanation: ∀y, (Book(y) ∧ Available(y)) → CanBorrow(y). Book(B7) aur Available(B7) dono sach hain, is liye CanBorrow(B7) nikalta hai: B7 li ja sakti hai.

items: ∀ se aam qaida: ∀x, Student(x) → Borrows(x, Book).
